principles: Separate evidence purposes rather than weaken either contract.
Keep real Git attribution distinct from independent reviewer execution.
Bind authority to current signed producer artifacts and reject incomplete or replayed bindings.
Limit the repair to the demonstrated inventory-launch deadlock.
drivers: B-7abb requires inventory completeness before REVIEW remediation but current shared dispatch requires an obsolete author identity.
Inventory receipts and topology certification have different consumers and must remain non-interchangeable.
The user requires RED before GREEN, independent review, real commit identity and local delivery.

options.name: Explicit inventory-purpose dispatch with current epoch binding
pros: Removes the unrelated business-author launch dependency only for inventory completeness.
Preserves existing topology provenance rules and makes purpose mechanically reviewable.
cons: Requires coordinated schema, dispatch, run, receipt-consumer and prompt regression coverage.

options.name: Accept arbitrary Git authors throughout topology provenance
pros: Would permit Harmonynet in more topology paths.
cons: Changes the independent business-author contract beyond the reported inventory defect; accepting a username alone cannot prove independence.

options.name: Restore role-named Git authors or bypass the critic
pros: Could suppress the immediate launch error.
cons: Violates the user identity requirement or mandatory independent review, so this option is rejected.

chosen: Explicit inventory-purpose dispatch with current epoch binding
rationale: Inventory-only review gets an explicit purpose and current signed epoch/wave/cutoff binding before any dispatch is accepted. The default topology path retains its current provenance checks and never falls back after failure. Existing role, run, read-evidence, classification and freshness validation remain mandatory; purpose must survive the producer-to-consumer path rather than live only in prose.

preMortem.scenario: Inventory purpose is used to mint topology certification.
preMortem.trigger: A caller reuses inventory dispatch or terminal evidence at a topology consumer.
preMortem.consequence: A limited completeness review is promoted to stronger authority.
preMortem.mitigation: Bind and verify purpose; test cross-purpose replay and retain unchanged topology provenance admission.

preMortem.scenario: An old or forged epoch launches an apparently current critic.
preMortem.trigger: Dispatch/run is replayed after wave advance, cancel, scope or material drift.
preMortem.consequence: Completeness receipt covers a different Finding set.
preMortem.mitigation: Read the canonical signed OPEN epoch, recheck epoch/wave/cutoff at run and receipt admission, and reject stale or tampered bindings.

preMortem.scenario: A synthetic test identity is reported as real independent review.
preMortem.trigger: Disposable fixture adapter identity leaks into project evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep fixture identities isolated and restored, and obtain real reviewer runs and any required actual-host assurance separately.
